summary: NHTSA found Chrysler's testing data less reliable than Ford's due to methodological deficiencies, and based the 8 percent testing effect primarily on Ford's data rather than Chrysler's.
text:
Chrysler's data are considered less reliable than Ford's because only 2 of 3 engine families were tested, and there were no tests of all

vehicle configurations or duplicate tests. After a careful analysis of these results, the NHTSA believes the manufacturers have demonstrated an 8 percent fuel economy effect and the average fuel economy standard has been reduced to reflect this effect. This effect reflects primarily the results of the Ford analysis.
opening_anchor: Chrysler's data are considered less reliable than Ford's because only 2 of 3 engine families were tested
closing_anchor: This effect reflects primarily the results of the Ford analysis.
